obligations.behavior: A rule with users [A, B] fires only for events whose data.author is A or B; an event by the actor's self_identity never fires it, even if listed; validate refuses a non-list users value.
obligations.source_text: Only allowlisted answerers advance the conversation: Jira comments by the operator's Jira user or a listed bot account; the culture-rules Jira account (the actor's self_identity) is never an answerer. Today Jira has no trigger filters (none registered for jira.*) and the author's accountId is not in event data (hooks.py:282-284 uses it only for self_authored), so the author must reach the event and be filterable.

obligations.seam: jira.issue.created trigger with the users filter
obligations.behavior: An issue opened by an unlisted reporter starts no run.
obligations.source_text: jira.read tags every comment and the issue itself with its author's accountId, and the author filter (c7) applies to jira.issue.created too, so a workflow can hand the agent only allowlisted authors' text: anyone with project access can open an issue or comment, and that text reaches an agent with tools on core (prompt injection).

obligations.seam: machine.command registered argv with a {key} param from trigger.data.key
obligations.behavior: The bound argv receives the validated issue key verbatim as one argument; a value with '/', '..' or NUL is refused before spawn; no shell is involved.
obligations.source_text: A registered runner command can keep durable per-key state across runs: machine.command runs registered argv in a fresh temp cwd with a minimal env (actors/code.py _sandboxed), so durable state is an absolute path argument built from a validated event field (e.g. trigger.data.key, matched by ISSUE_KEY_RE in hooks.py); the directory layout is the configured wrapper's business, not culture-rules'.

obligations.seam: BridgeAgentActor step (culture_rules/actors/agent.py) with a working_path input
obligations.behavior: Forwards repo, head_branch, head_sha, model and an optional working path to the bridge; an actor pinned read-only refuses a step asking for another sandbox (sandbox_locked); the agent's returned output is available to later steps unchanged.
obligations.source_text: A workflow step can bind a bridge agent actor (any model, here Fable 5.2 by configuration) in either of two generic modes: (a) output-only, read-only on the repo, its output plain step output that later steps (e.g. a registered machine.command) consume; (b) operating, the bridge running on core with tools and a writable working path given by the step. The bridge needs repo, head_branch and a commit head_sha (actors/agent.py:349,703-808) and pins sandbox/mode per actor (agent.py:715-725).

obligations.behavior: Runs claude -p with Bash limited to named commands and one writable working path; any checkout change or write outside the path fails the run; push is always denied; --model passes through.
obligations.source_text: Cross-repo (cultureagent): the Claude bridge gains an operating role for mode (b): the checkout stays unchanged (the reviewer's baseline check), Bash is limited to named commands, and one per-invocation writable working path is allowed, plus a model name (Fable 5.2). Today it has only read-only (no Bash, no writes, checkout change fails the run) and workspace-write (edits the worktree, never pushes) roles, its tool lists are per deployment (fixer_allowed_tools, config.py:211-212), and its only writable path is worktrees_root (cultureagent bridges/claude/backend.py:1-25, README.md:38-43).

obligations.seam: Jira custom field → bridge step repo input; default-branch head lookup
obligations.behavior: A workflow can map a configured field value to repo and obtain a 40-hex head_sha for its default branch with generic steps only; a repo outside the bridge allowlist is refused by the bridge (403).
obligations.source_text: Generic repo context for a bridge step: a Jira read can return configured fields (a custom field naming the repo) so a workflow can map it, and a step can resolve a repo's default branch and head sha; what to do when the repo is missing is configuration.

obligations.seam: library.push with content_path under a content_root on core
obligations.behavior: Uploads the md file as kind spec, visibility private; the stored bytes equal the file; a kind the actor does not list is refused.
obligations.source_text: library.push can publish a md file from a runner-produced path as kind spec, private: culture-library already has kind spec (culture_library/core/models.py:12-25); the library actor's kinds and its key gain spec by configuration (docs/actors/library.md); no repodocs route.

obligations.behavior: A round that ends failed runs the configured jira.comment once, with run.error.code readable in its body.
obligations.source_text: A failed round tells the operator: the round rule's on_failure action (model/rule.py:64) posts one Jira comment with the failure code, so a bridge timeout or a refused command never leaves the issue silently waiting.

obligations.behavior: After max_attempts admitted runs for jiraconv:<key>, further comments start no run and the skip is recorded.
obligations.source_text: Rounds are bounded by the generic per-key attempt budget (model/rule.py:99-112, max_attempts on the issue's concurrency key), set by configuration, so a conversation cannot loop without end.

obligations.behavior: Two comments arriving during one round produce exactly one follow-up run, whose jira.read sees both comments.
obligations.source_text: The conversation is a chain of rule firings, not one waiting run: jira.issue.created starts round one, and jira.comment.created on the same issue (concurrency_key like jiraconv:{trigger.data.key}) runs the next round; the wait step is time-only (model/validate.py:686-740) and a human ask is answered only through the API (actors/human.py:166), with no Jira bridge.

obligations.behavior: No string 'devague' appears in culture_rules/, tests/ or web/src; a new jira literal outside extensions/jira fails the test unless pinned in APP_LITERALS_ALLOWED.
obligations.source_text: culture-rules implements generics only and cannot tell what devague is: devague (its CLI, ids, obligations, answer grammar, export) is purely configuration — a registered runner command, the agent's step instruction, and live rules/workflows — never code, literals or tests in culture_rules/.

obligations.seam: Configured core wrapper around devague (outside the repo)
obligations.behavior: Agent-originated moves are always recorded proposed; confirm/reject/resolve/oblige --confirm run only from the reply step citing an allowlisted comment id; a post-run check refuses any new confirmation not traced to a reply.
obligations.source_text: The operating agent cannot adjudicate: in mode (b) only the reply step (driven by an allowlisted comment) may confirm, reject or resolve, and every agent-made record lands as a proposal. Risk: devague capture defaults to --origin user, which auto-confirms, and the agent could run confirm itself or edit the frame JSON.

obligations.behavior: No run pushes a branch, opens a PR or changes a repo checkout; the only publication is one library.push.
obligations.source_text: This flow changes no repo and opens no PR: it ends with a spec in the library. Turning a spec into a PR is a later culture-rules flow; today culture-rules can read a PR (github.pr) and merge one behind an operator click and one-time code (github.merge) but has no kind that opens one (extensions/github/__init__.py:32-34).
